From: Ian Chen <ian.chen@orionanalytics.com>
To: demos@redwood-inference.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Demo request: Dedicated capacity - throughput & latency

Hi —

We just signed up via the self-serve demo flow and selected the Dedicated capacity option. A few details up front so the demo can focus on what matters:
- Workload: conversational search + reranking for user queries (mix of short prompts and multi-turn).
- Target sustained throughput: 400–600 QPS during business hours; burst to ~1,000 QPS for 10–15 minutes.
- Latency target: P95 < 250ms for single-turn responses (token-limited), P95 < 350ms for short multi-turn sessions.
- Data sensitivity: customer PII, need KMS integration and audit logs.

I attached a short capacity worksheet (capacity_requirements.xlsx) with more details.

Would like a short walkthrough of Dedicated capacity and a technical check on batching/latency tradeoffs. Availability next week is flexible mornings PT.

Thanks,
Ian Chen
Engineering Lead — Orion Analytics
ian.chen@orionanalytics.com

Attachment: capacity_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

- Tue 27 Apr, 9:00–9:45am

Also, do you have an internal SLA definition for P95 latency we should try to hit in the demo?

Tessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We’ll take Tue 27 Apr, 10:30–11:15am PT. A couple notes so Marcus and Ben can scope the session:
- We expect a single model family (same weights) but two serving profiles: low-latency short answers (~80% of traffic) and high-quality long-form responses (~20%). Routing is at the application layer; we'd like to understand how Redwood handles profile-aware batching and autoscale.
- Bursts to 1,000 QPS are real (marketing spikes) and typically last 5–20 mins; we’d like to understand warm-burst strategies (prewarmed capacity, burst credits, fallback routing).
- Security: we require customer-managed KMS and Audit logs to feed into our SIEM. If you can include a slide on Private/VPC options and KMS support that'd be great.

I attached a SOC 2 summary we can share internally — hopefully useful for procurement.

See you Tue — Priya joined on this thread for procurement coordination.
